newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: NOVA LEADS IN 1ST CZECH PEOPLEMETER TEST.
newsitem.headline: NOVA LEADS IN 1ST CZECH PEOPLEMETER TEST.

text.p: Czech commercial station TV Nova, a unit of Central European Media Enterprises Ltd. (CME), averaged a 54 percent share of viewers aged 15 and over in the first electronic "peoplemeter" measurements in early June.

However the data released on Monday by Taylor Nelson AGB Media Facts showed a lower share for Nova than diary-based demographics used in recent years which showed it maintaining an average viewership of about 70 percent of households.

The Taylor Nelson metres electronically gather data on the viewing habits of 660 Czech households in 15-minute intevals each day, which is downloaded to a central computer in Prague for processing and use by the participating stations.

The largest public broadcasting channel Ceska Televise 1 (CT1) averaged a 27 percent share during the June 2-6 peoplemeter sample while the commercial channel Prima had an eight percent share and the arts-oriented CT2 had six percent.
In the prime time hours of 7.30-10.00 p.m., Nova's average share dipped to 52 percent, while CT1's grew to 31 percent and Prima and CT2's share remained the same as the overall average.
Nova posted 19 of the top 20 most highly rated programmes for the week with its main news and sports broadcasts accounting for 10 of the top 13 slots with viewer shares ranging from 60-72 percent.

Nova was launched in early 1994 by New York cosmetic scion Ronald Lauder's CME as post-Communist Europe's first nationwide commercial station, and quickly dominated Czech television with a mix of American serials, action films, and tabloid news.
Nova's Sunday 7.30 p.m. newscast was the highest-rated programme for the week with a 35.7 rating and a 72 percent share or 3.1 million viewers in a country of 10.3 million.
The U.S. series "Dallas" was second with a 35.7 rating, 70 share and 3.08 million viewers in a Thursday prime time slot.
Only CT1's home video show "Nevahej a Toc" ("Don't Hesitate and Shoot") made it in the top 20, placing eighth with 2.52 million viewers and a 63 percent share.
